title: Constructibility under the normalized native adic encoding
statement: Fix a prime l [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let T be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let M be a native adic sheaf on T: a module object in sheaves of vector spaces over the locally finite continuous algebraic-closure coefficient sheaf, as in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let R_T be the pulled-back bounded-image condensed algebraic closure of Q_l [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let E_T be the normalized native encoding [lem-sf-native-adic-encoding-ordinary-operations]: forget to abelian module sheaves and restrict scalars through its canonical coefficient isomorphism. Then M is native constructible (locally on T a finite constructible locally closed partition with pro-etale locally finite-free restrictions) if and only if E_T(M) is a constructible R_T-module [def-sfb-constructible-module] (a finite constructible immersed stratification on which the raw inverse-image module is locally finitely presented). This includes empty T and zero or varying finite ranks.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.8. Agent-formulated comparison of the two concrete constructibility predicates, using the already stated local-presentation/local-freeness characterization.

proof.text: The canonical coefficient isomorphism identifies the native regular module with the condensed regular module after encoding. An additive equivalence preserves finite biproducts, so it identifies every finite-free module, including rank zero. Restriction of scalars along a ring isomorphism preserves and reflects finite freeness; a finite-free module has a finite cokernel presentation by the zero map. These elementary module-object facts are proved as private helpers.

For a native lisse sheaf, take its pro-etale finite-free trivializing presieve and reduce its cover index universe using the smallness of the pro-etale precoverage. On each member apply pullComparison, the encoded trivialization, and the finite-free comparison from step 1. The invertible coefficient pullback and extendScalarsIsoComapInv identify the condensed pullback with raw inverse image, giving local finite presentation. Conversely apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality] on the topologically Noetherian scheme to obtain a cover with finite-free condensed pullbacks. PullComparison, the inverse finite-free comparison and full faithfulness of encoding lift these to native trivializations.

Every immersed stratum of T has Noetherian underlying space, since its inclusion is a topological embedding. Thus step 2 applies on each stratum. The pullback comparison and the invertible coefficient pullback identify native lisse restriction with local finite presentation of the raw condensed inverse-image module. Transport finite presentation with the proved localFinitePresentation_of_iso, localFinitePresentation_comap and localFinitePresentation_of_comap helpers of [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback].

A Noetherian scheme is qcqs. By [lem-sf-native-adic-qcqs-stratification], native constructibility gives a finite global immersed stratification with constructible images and lisse restrictions. Enumerate its finite index type by Fin n, retain the actual stratum schemes and immersions, and apply step 3 on each. This is exactly the condensed constructibility witness. Conversely a condensed constructible stratification gives native lisse restrictions by step 3. Its disjoint images and union provide the required unique covering stratum, so it is a native stratified-lisse witness and hence native constructible. The construction permits empty strata and empty index types.

lean.statement:
theorem encoding_constructible_iff {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian T]
    (M : AdicSheaf l T) :
    IsAdicConstructibleSheaf M ↔
      IsConstructibleModuleObject (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj l) T)
        ((NativeEncoding.encoding l T).obj M)
